spans.s: + अन्न मिष्ट- + अन्न, n. a mixture of sugar and acids, etc., eaten with bread or rice.
+ कर्तृ मिष्ट- + कर्तृ, m. a confectioner.

1. मिष् मिष् (probably for मिक्ष्, and akin to मिह्), i. 1, Par. To sprinkle.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. मिष्ट.
 1.
. Sweet, Pañc. 119, 7. n. A fine dish, Böhtl. Ind.

2. मिष् मिष्, i. 6, Par. (properly To wink, to contract the eyelids, cf. मील्, क्ष्मील्, श्मील्, स्मील्, and स्मि).
 1. To look at angrily,

(हरामि मिषतां वस्, I shall take [her] while you are looking on angrily, i. e. in spite of you).
 2. † To contend, to resist.
 --With the prep. उद् उद्,
 1. To open one's eyes,

.
 --With प्रत्युद् प्रति-उद्, To break forth, Daśak. in

.
 --With नि नि, [] To shut one's eyes, to wink,

.
 --Cf. Lat. miser; μῖσος, probably also μύω, cf. ὄμματα, συμ-μεμυκότα, ἀναμεμυκότα; Lat. micare.
† मिस् मिस्, i. 4, Par. To go.

मिश्र्, and † मिस्र् मिस्र्, i. 10 (rather a denomin. derived from मिश्र), Par. To mix, Śāk. d. 30. मिश्रित,
 1. Mixed, Pañc. 215, 2.
 2. Respected (i. e. मिश्र + इत, cf. मिश्र).
 --With the prep. वि वि, To put in disorder,

मिश्र, i. e. मिश् (perhaps for मिक्ष्, desider. of मिह्, without red., cf. मिह् with सम्), + र,
 I. adj. Mixed, Böhtl. Ind.

.
 II. n. Mixing.
 III. m.
 1. An elephant.
 2. A respectable person, Sir,
; in this sense it is a common affix to nouns,

.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Lat. miscere; O.H.G. miscjan; A.S. miscan; μίσγω, μίγνυμι.

मिश्र + क,
 I. m.
 1. A mixer.
 2. An adulterator of commodities, a mixer of bad wares with good ones,

.
 II. n. A grove of paradise.

मिस्ह् + अ,
 I. m. Emulation.
 II. n. Fraud.
